ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, AC is the diagonal of rectangle ABCD. Fold side AB along AE so that point B falls on point M on AC, and fold side CD along CF so that point D falls on point N on AC. It is easy to prove that quadrilateral AECF is a parallelogram. When $\angle BAE$ is how many degrees, the quadrilateral AECF becomes a rhombus.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: When $\angle BAE = 30^\circ$, the quadrilateral AECF is a rhombus,\\
Reason: It is known from folding that $\angle BAE = \angle CAE = 30^\circ$,\\
$\because \angle B = 90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle ACE = 90^\circ - 30^\circ - 30^\circ = 30^\circ$,\\
which means $\angle CAE = \angle ACE$,\\
$\therefore EA = EC$,\\
$\because$ the quadrilateral AECF is a parallelogram,\\
$\therefore$ the quadrilateral AECF is a rhombus,\\
Therefore, the answer is: $\boxed{30^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a rectangle ABCD, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, D is at the upper right; AC is the diagonal from A to C. Point E is on the bottom side BC, point F is on the top side AD, AE and CF are connected, and quadrilateral AECF is shown as a parallelogram. The dashed lines indicate that the folded points M and N fall on the diagonal AC, where folding AB along AE makes B fall to M on AC, and folding CD along CF makes D fall to N on AC. Reasoning: Let θ=∠BAE. In the first fold, A remains fixed on the crease AE, and B falls to M with respect to the crease AE, so ray AB is folded to AM, and AE bisects ∠BAM. Also because M is on AC, AM and AC are collinear, and ∠BAM=∠BAC. Thus ∠BAC=2θ, and ∠EAC=∠BAC−∠BAE=θ. It is known that AECF is a parallelogram. If it becomes a rhombus, then adjacent sides AE=EC, so triangle AEC is an isosceles triangle, and the base angles are equal: ∠EAC=∠ACE. Since E is on BC, CE and CB are collinear, so ∠ACE=∠ACB. In rectangle ABCD, △ABC is a right triangle, ∠ABC=90°, so ∠ACB=90°−∠BAC=90°−2θ. From ∠EAC=∠ACE, obtain θ=90°−2θ, solving gives 3θ=90°, so θ=30°.
